R9 Radial Engine

Design notes for the nine-cylinder master and articulating rod crank train modelled in Fusion as R9 Engine Assembly. They cover the layout decisions, the knuckle pin tuning, crankshaft balance, the structure of the CAD model and the checks run on it.

2Layout and rod length

The rod length was set by packaging rather than by angularity. With nine cylinders on 40 deg spacing, two adjacent 150 mm pistons stop clearing each other once the wrist pin comes inside a radius of about 219 mm, and the skirts sit 55 mm below the pin. A 300 mm master rod put the pistons at BDC too close to the crank axis for the skirts to clear, so the master rod went to 380 mm. That puts the wrist pin at 295 mm at BDC and the skirt bottom at 240 mm, where adjacent pistons have 26.3 mm between them.

The longer rod also lowers the master rod swing to 12.9 deg either side of the cylinder axis, which keeps the piston side load and the angular travel of the link rods relative to the master rod small.

The cylinder hold-down flanges and the inner barrel fins would still meet their neighbours, so each cylinder carries two flats 2 mm off the bisector between cylinders (feature Fin clearance). The resulting gap between neighbouring fin stacks is 4 mm.

3Articulated rod kinematics

Only cylinder 1 runs on a true slider crank. The link rods pivot on knuckle pins carried by the master rod big end, and the big end rocks as the crank turns. With all knuckle pins on one circle at exactly 40 deg spacing, each link-rod cylinder ends up with a slightly different TDC height, a slightly longer stroke than the master cylinder, and a TDC that is offset in crank angle. The TDC height spread matters most, because it sets the compression ratio of each cylinder.

Each knuckle pin was given its own radius a_k and angular offset d_k from the 40 deg station. These sixteen values were found by least squares on the closed-form solution, sampled at 0.25 deg over a revolution, with weights of 4 on TDC height error, 2 on stroke error, 0.2 on TDC timing and a small penalty keeping the pins near the nominal circle.

master: s1 = r cos(t) + sqrt(L^2 - r^2 sin^2(t)), beta = atan2(-r sin t, s1 - r cos t) pin k: K_k = C + a_k (sin(beta + 40k + d_k), cos(beta + 40k + d_k)) piston: s_k = K_k.u_k + sqrt(l^2 - |K_k|^2 + (K_k.u_k)^2)
Knuckle pin layoutTDC height spreadMax strokeTDC timing offset
Equal pins, 80 mm circle, 40 deg spacing2.40 mm170.57 mm±3.50 deg
Tuned pins (as modelled)<0.001 mm170.00 mm±3.75 deg

The tuning trades a quarter of a degree of extra timing offset for equal compression and stroke on every cylinder. The timing offset is fixed for each cylinder, so it would be taken out in the ignition and valve timing.

4Crankshaft balance

In a single-row radial with three or more cylinders, the primary reciprocating forces add to a vector of constant magnitude (N/2) mrec r ω² that turns with the crank. A counterweight can therefore cancel the whole primary force along with the rotating mass at the crankpin, which an in-line engine cannot do.

Mass at the crankpinkgBasis
Rotating: master rod big end, knuckle pins, link rod big ends18.87Rods split by centre of mass position between their eyes
Reciprocating, cylinder 16.07Piston, pin and master rod small-end share
Reciprocating, cylinders 2 to 94.40 eachPiston, pin and link rod small-end share
Primary equivalent, N/2 x mean mrec20.63
Required crank unbalance, opposite the pin3358 kg.mm(18.87 + 20.63) x 85 mm
Modelled crankshaft3370 kg.mmRead from Fusion mass properties

The counterweight is a 150 deg sector whose radius is driven by CounterweightRadius. It was converged on the CAD body by a secant search on that parameter and rounded to 217.5 mm, leaving 0.4 % overbalance. The secondary forces and the variation caused by the articulated rods are not balanced; that is normal for this layout and would be handled by mounts and, if needed, a dynamic damper.

5Cylinder

The cylinder is one body built the way it would be drawn by hand: a revolved blank, one barrel fin and one head fin each patterned along the axis (34 at 7 mm, 12 at 7.5 mm), port bosses, rocker box bosses, then the bore cut up from the base to the deck and the chamber revolved out of the head. The bore diameter, deck height and chamber height all follow user parameters. Intake ports face the rear and exhaust ports face the front.

6CAD model structure

Components

Eight components, each with its own origin on the crank axis or on its own pin centre: Crankcase, Cylinder, Crankshaft, Master Rod, Link Rod, Piston, Wrist Pin and Knuckle Pin. Repeated parts are instances of a single component, so a change to one cylinder or one piston carries to all of them. Cylinder numbers follow the usual convention, clockwise from the rear with number 1 at the top. Link Rod instance n belongs to cylinder n+1, and Knuckle Pin instance n likewise.

Timeline

The timeline is grouped by component, followed by Instances, the ground, the as-assembled position, Joints and Rigid groups. Sketches use connected geometry and true arcs. The master rod pin layout, the crank web and the link rod pin layout are fully constrained.

Stroke, rod lengths and deck height are layout values fixed by the study above. They update the parts, but the joints were made with the parts assembled at crank angle 0, so a change to any of them needs the assembly re-seated and the kinematic check rerun.

Joints and how to drive it

The crankcase is grounded and locked to the nine cylinders in a rigid group. The crankshaft turns in the case on Main bearing; the master rod turns on Crankpin; each link rod turns on its knuckle pin and its wrist pin; each piston slides in its bore. The master rod and its knuckle pins form one rigid group and each piston is grouped with its wrist pin. All nine slider-crank loops are closed, so the mechanism has one degree of freedom. Drag the crankshaft, or set the angle of Main bearing (positive is clockwise seen from the rear, the normal direction for a tractor engine).

8Scope and open items

This is a crank train layout. It is complete enough to check kinematics, packaging and balance, and it is not a detailed design. The following are not modelled and are the next items to take on.

  • Open Valve train: cam ring, tappets, pushrods and rockers. The rocker boxes are bosses only.
  • Open Bearings: main bearings, big-end shells and knuckle pin bushes are represented by bore allowances.
  • Open Induction, supercharger, ignition and the accessory drive in the rear case.
  • Open Propeller reduction gearing. The propeller flange is on the crankshaft.
  • Open Structural checks: crankpin and web stresses, rod buckling, cylinder hold-down loads. Gas loads have not been applied.
  • Open Link rod to skirt clearance on cylinders 5 and 6 is 4.6 mm. A skirt relief notch or a slimmer link rod shank near the big eye would give more margin.
  • Open Ring land and valve pocket volumes, which will pull the compression ratio slightly below 6.8.
